== Course of events ==

After the truth of Oz's nature comes to light, the once-mighty figure withdraws alone, no longer able to maintain the pretense that had governed his dealings with those who sought him out. Left to himself, Oz privately admits that he is a humbug, dropping the guise entirely now that there is no one left to deceive. Yet the admission brings him no relief, for it exposes a deeper problem he cannot easily solve: Dorothy still needs a way back to Kansas, and Oz has no idea how to accomplish it.

The worry that follows is bound entirely to Dorothy and her wish to return home. Unlike the requests he has learned to satisfy through illusion and trickery, sending her back to Kansas is not a matter he can resolve with the same tools. His private doubt marks a turning point: the humbug who could produce convincing effects for others finds himself without an answer for the one problem that matters most to Dorothy.
